compiled_state.title: [cycle_ledger]: reconstruct_from_pr_comments reads /pulls/.../comments instead of /issues/.../comments -> cycle counter pinned
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## 1. Technical Environment
* Plugin Version: dso v1.17.9
* code_version: 22e4881f0022631b65d3af01acf6303893042a46
* Discovered during: SC10 evidence sprint (story c4f1-c18d-0000-4001, epic b575-ac1c-f720-4839) — multi-cycle arbiter dispatch attempt on PR #265
* Related: bug 9788 (cycle marker writer/parser format mismatch) — fix in PR #263 fixed the WRITER but the RECONSTRUCTION endpoint is still wrong.

## 2. Incident Overview

### Expected Behavior

`cycle_ledger.reconstruct_from_pr_comments(pr_number, repo)` should rebuild the cycle ledger from `DSO-Review-Cycle:` markers posted to the PR. The runner's writer (`runner.py:1796`) posts these markers via `gh pr comment <num> --body`, which writes to the PR's **issue conversation** (the `/issues/{n}/comments` endpoint). The reconstruction must read the same endpoint to find the markers it is meant to reconstruct from.

### Actual Behavior

`cycle_ledger.py:255`:
```python
cmd = ["gh", "api", f"repos/{repo}/pulls/{pr_number}/comments", "--paginate"]
```

This is the **PR review-thread comments** endpoint (line-attached review comments), NOT the issue conversation endpoint. The two endpoints return entirely disjoint comment sets. DSO-Review-Cycle markers live in `/issues/.../comments` (issue conversation); the reconstruction reads `/pulls/.../comments` (review thread). Result: reconstruction silently returns zero cycles regardless of how many markers exist.

Downstream effect: cycle_dispatcher.next_action sees `cycles=[]` → last_cycle=None → cycle_num=1 on every CI rerun → DISPATCH_ARBITER (cycle_num >= max_cycles=4) is unreachable from any live PR.

Same root cause as bug 9788 (writer/parser format mismatch) — the writer side was fixed in PR #263 but the reconstruction endpoint side was never aligned with where the writer actually posts.

### Empirical evidence

PR #265 (sandbox SC10 PR, branch sc10-step2-sanity-20260521-191936):
- Cycle 1 ran (initial push), posted `DSO-Review-Cycle: 1` marker to issue conversation (visible via `gh api repos/.../issues/265/comments`).
- gh run rerun → attempt 2. Compute-DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE step computed env=2 (counting review-thread `finding 1/` headers). Runner reconstructed ledger from `/pulls/265/comments` → 0 cycles → fell back to DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE env=2 → posted cycle 2 marker.
- gh run rerun → attempt 3. Same path: ledger empty, env=2 again (count of finding-1 headers unchanged because no new findings posted in attempt 2 review path), runner attempted cycle 2 again (NOT cycle 3). Cycle marker writer's dedup logic at line 1758 saw existing cycle 2 marker and PATCHed it in place. No new cycle 3 marker.
- gh api confirmed: PR #265 has exactly 2 DSO-Review-Cycle markers in issue conversation; PR review thread returns 1 finding-1 header.
- cycle_dispatcher next_action() returned cycle_num=1 on every rerun, dispatching back to DISPATCH_NEXT, never reaching DISPATCH_ARBITER.

## 3. Root Cause

`reconstruct_from_pr_comments` reads the wrong GitHub API endpoint. It is the dual of bug 9788's writer-side fix — the writer was aligned to issue comments but the reader was left on review-thread comments.

## 4. Suggested Fix

`plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/cycle_ledger.py:255`:
- Change: `f"repos/{repo}/pulls/{pr_number}/comments"` → `f"repos/{repo}/issues/{pr_number}/comments"`

Add a round-trip integration test: write a cycle marker via the runner's writer path, then call reconstruct_from_pr_comments on the same PR — assert reconstruction returns the marker.

## 5. Acceptance Criteria

- The reconstruction MUST hit the same GitHub API endpoint that the writer (`runner._post_cycle_marker_comment`) posts to. The two MUST be derived from one shared constant or helper to prevent recurrence.
- After fix, on a synthetic 4-cycle PR, the cycle_dispatcher MUST reach cycle_num=4 and dispatch the arbiter (consistent with SC10 evidence requirements on epic b575).
- A regression test MUST validate writer-reader endpoint parity (assert the constant or helper is shared).

## 6. Discovery Provenance

Discovered 2026-05-21 22:30 UTC while attempting to capture SC10 evidence on PR #265. Confirmed empirically by querying both endpoints — issue comments contained the cycle markers, review-thread comments did not. Code inspection at `cycle_ledger.py:255` confirmed the endpoint mismatch.
